findings.title: Config-injection design verified against all surface call sites; worktree scoping claim holds
findings.description: The design's component table names four production instantiations. Verified: `next.ts:26`, `status.ts:119`, `workflowTools.ts:154` and `:200` are exactly the navigator construction sites (no others). The "worktree scope inherited for free" claim is accurate: `next.ts` resolves via `resolveProjectWorktree` → `resolveProject(store, id, worktreeId)`, `status.ts:146-151` does the same, and both MCP workflow tools call `resolveProject(store, resolvedId, args.worktreeId)` — all of which route through `applyWorktreeOverlay`, which rewrites `projectPath` to the worktree path. So `ConfigManager(project.projectPath)` resolves project-scoped review config at worktree scope, matching the design's Interfaces-Required bullet and 180's resolution chain.

findings.title: Conservative-by-default is structurally preserved and matches the arch's behavioral invariant
findings.description: Optional constructor parameter + "config undefined or `review_enabled` false ⇒ don't even look for a review artifact," verified by a regression test rather than inspection, matches the arch's "Conservative by default" and "Extend, don't replace" principles and its insertion-point constraint (the reserved `LIFECYCLE: review-gate` branch sits before `complete-advance` in the source, exactly where the design fills it). The arch states no latency/throughput NFRs; the one behavioral invariant it does state (no change when gating off) is restated here with a concrete test target. TD-7's additive-only recommendation vocabulary correctly preserves the `NextAction` return type the arch requires for Amoeba.

findings.title: TD-4, the 244 retirement, and the STATUS/910 split resolve items the parent plan explicitly assigned to this slice
findings.description: The slice plan says "the design (Phase 4) makes that call" for both the inert `review_type` keys and whether per-gate `threshold` survives — TD-4 makes both calls within the sanctioned options and flags the removal alternative for the PM. The 244 retirement matches the plan's note verbatim. The `STATUS` const introduction matches maintenance slice 910's plan entry, which states "slice 241 introduces the STATUS constant for its own new code; this slice completes the sweep" — the dependency direction (910 depends on 241) is correct, as are 240 → 241 → {242, 243}. Proportionality is sound: nothing outside the plan entry is added, nothing assigned is dropped, and excluded scope (242/243/910/score) is explicit.

findings.title: Review-artifact I/O failure modes are explicitly enumerated with a no-silent-pass strategy
findings.description: The absent artifact → `pending`; present-but-unparseable → `UNKNOWN` → `review_unknown_as`, never surfaced as `pending` — is exactly the arch's "must not silently pass" requirement, and the design keeps the present-vs-absent distinction from collapsing. The `parseFrontmatter` never-throws contract the design leans on is verified in source (`frontmatterParser.ts:7,10,46`). The decision matrix matches the shipped config enums (`['pass','concerns']` / `['fail','concerns','pass']` in `ConfigKeys.ts`) and the arch's verdict vocabulary.

findings.title: The pre-slice-plan (arch) gate has no working routing mechanism: the reserved branch is unreachable when there is no active slice, and first-run context intercepts the boundary
findings.description: TD-3 says the new statuses flow through `getStatus()`/`activeSlice` and that `getNext()`'s reserved `review-gate` branch maps them to `review`/`blocked`. That mechanism cannot deliver the arch boundary: in `WorkflowNavigator.ts`, every no-active-slice path returns from *inside* the `GUARD: no-active-slice` block (`:98-190`) — including `detectFirstRunContext` (`:326-425`), whose FR-3b branch (`:384-393`) returns "Architecture document exists. Advance to Phase 3 and create a slice plan" for precisely the state the arch gate must intercept (arch exists ∧ no slice plan ∧ Phase 2). When there is no active slice, `activeSlice` is null, so no `pending-review` status can be attached or routed, and the reserved branch is never reached. The design says "extend the no-active-slice/pre-slice-plan path" (`:33`, `:57`) but never specifies an insertion point, the recommendation shape for that path, or precedence over first-run guidance. Unmet requirements: the arch's Overview ("recommends `pending-review` or `review-failed` instead of recommending an advance") and this design's own Success Criteria ("the same clears/pending/failed behavior holds at the … arch boundaries"). The design must specify where in the no-active-slice cascade the gate evaluates and how the review/blocked recommendation is produced there.

findings.title: The pre-slice-plan review lookup index is undefined — there is no slice index at that boundary
findings.description: The boundary→signal table gives the *condition* ("arch file exists, no slice plan") but not the *index* for the review lookup. `detectDocuments` matches reviews as `{index}-review.{reviewType}.*.md` (`documentDetector.ts:87-97`), and at the arch boundary `slice.index` is null. The design's own band-mismatch precedent shows arch files carry their own numeric prefix that can differ from a slice's (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:120-127` compares `extractSliceIndex(project.fileArch)` against the slice's hundred-block as distinct bands), and the 240 fixture convention named an arch review `100-review.arch.*.md` for the 100-family. Which index derives the lookup — `extractSliceIndex(project.fileArch)`, the initiative base index, or something else — is unstated, so the Success Criterion "the correct review type is looked for automatically" (`arch` row) is unimplementable as specified, and slice 242 (which reuses `positionToReviewType` plus detection) inherits the hole. Name the rule and add it to the per-boundary tests.

findings.title: The pre-implementation (tasks) gate trigger is self-contradictory and as written fires throughout implementation, not before it
findings.description: The Overview table (`:25`) says the signal is "task file exists, **not implemented**"; the boundary table (`:138`) says "task file exists, **not complete**." These differ materially: in `deriveSliceStatus`, `in-implementation` covers every state from 1/N to (N-1)/N checked (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:493-496`), so implementing "not complete" makes the tasks gate fire for the entire implementation phase — a slice at 3/5 checked with no tasks review flips to `pending-review` and `cf next` recommends a review instead of "Continue implementation — 2 tasks remaining." That contradicts the arch's transition name (`pre-implementation` — the tasks review gates the *start* of implementation) and TD-7's rationale examples, which assume the complete/code case. Pin the signal to "task file exists ∧ zero tasks completed" (or a not-started inferred status — note `deriveSliceStatus` never produces a distinct 'not-started' slice status, so the distinction must be made on `taskProgress.completed`), and add a mid-implementation no-fire test to the per-boundary coverage.

findings.title: New config-read I/O path has no failure-mode handling, violating the arch's fail-fast principle and the gating-off "byte-for-byte identical" claim
findings.description: Once a `ConfigManager` is injected, `resolveGateConfig` makes `cf next`/`cf status`/`workflow_next` read `.context-forge.toml` on every call — including when gating is off (`review_enabled` must be read to know it's off). `ConfigManager.get` → `readToml` throws on malformed TOML (`ConfigManager.ts:12-20` swallows only ENOENT). The design's failure-mode enumeration covers the review file but not the config file. Worse, the natural integration point is inside `deriveSliceStatus`'s existing `try { … } catch { return base; }` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:461-499`), where a config-read throw silently degrades to `no-active-slice` — a silent fallback, which CLAUDE.md forbids and the arch's "Fail-fast on configuration errors … surfaced immediately, not a silent pass or silent block" principle explicitly prohibits. It also undermines the Overview's "gating off ⇒ behavior byte-for-byte identical" guarantee (`:31`): today the navigator reads no config, so a malformed TOML is invisible to `cf next`; after 241 it is not, and the gating-off regression test (which uses a stub or no config) cannot catch it. State the handling explicitly: propagate the error to the CLI/MCP error boundary (fail-fast), or catch with an explicit warning and a documented gating-off policy — and scope the "identical" guarantee to valid config.

findings.title: The arch's parse-failure rationale requirement is silently dropped by the never-throws parser choice
findings.description: The arch (240-arch §Technical Considerations, "File-read failure modes") requires: "The rationale returned to the caller names the parse failure explicitly." The design adopts `parseFrontmatter`'s collapse of read/parse errors into `{ found: false, data: {} }` as "exactly the behavior the gate needs" — correct for the verdict decision (TD-2 `:216` keeps present-but-unparseable ≠ pending), but it discards the information the arch says the rationale must carry: TD-1's `normalizeVerdict(raw: string | undefined)` and the data flow (`:161`) never plumb `FrontmatterResult.found` (or file existence) forward, so "unreadable/malformed file" is indistinguishable from "file with no frontmatter block," and TD-7's rationale spec (`:268`) names only review type, verdict, and threshold. As written, an arch requirement is unmet without being acknowledged. Either plumb `found`/existence into the gate result so the rationale can distinguish the cases, or explicitly restate/drop the arch's rationale clause as a design decision for the PM — don't leave it silently unmet.

findings.title: The `workflow_status` tool description enumerates a closed status set that this slice's own edit makes stale
findings.description: `workflowTools.ts`'s `workflow_status` description enumerates "(needs-design, needs-tasks, in-implementation, complete)" — after 241 it is incomplete, and the tool is interface surface for downstream AI consumers, not just user docs. Documentation is correctly deferred to 243, but since 241 already edits `workflowTools.ts` (its component table), folding the two new values into that description string in the same change would avoid shipping a knowingly stale contract for a slice cycle. Minor; 243 coverage is an acceptable fallback.
